Proposed sensitivity & approval mechanics (summary):

Assumptions: baseline market GPU list price = $2.50/token-equivalent (index proxy); baseline retail rate used in our quote = $2.00/token-equivalent after standard discounts. Committed pool: 120 GPUs, 24 months.

Sensitivity scenarios (impact on net effective rate):
- Market price -30%: index = $1.75 -> we can maintain base discount; net rate improves by ~8% relative to baseline quote. No additional approval required.
- Market price -15%: index = $2.12 -> recommend passing some savings back; auto-tier reduces customer rate by ~5%. Requires AE sign-off + sales ops notification.
- Market price +15%: index = $2.88 -> pressure on margin; to preserve economic neutrality we propose a GPU-index escalator where above +10% move we reduce discounting by X points to protect margin. Any requested price uplift (customer-facing) or reduction in committed units requires Sales Manager + Finance review.
- Market price +30%: index = $3.25 -> triggers executive review; discounts capped and customer offered capacity re-phasing options (e.g., adjust tenor or allow short-term bursting at market rates). VP Sales + Finance approval required for any >18% discount.

Approval table (proposal):
- <= 5% off baseline: AE approval
- >5% and <= 12%: Sales Manager approval (karthik) + Sales Ops notice
- >12% and <= 18%: Sales Director approval (ben) + Finance sign-off
- >18%: VP Sales + CFO approval (requires exec exception ticket INF-4021)

Attachments: zephyr-pricing-sensitivity.pdf (detailed numbers + waterfall). Please flag anything I missed.

Thanks,
Lauren

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Zephyr Health — reserve-tier sizing, GPU price ladder & approval checklist

Lauren — thanks for the draft. A couple of pragmatic asks from my side:

1) Make the index math explicit in the PDF: show the formula we use to convert GPU list price -> token-equivalent index and then how that maps to customer per-token rate. Without the formula procurement will push back.
2) For rebalancing: we’ll allow monthly SKU rebalancing up to +/- 25% of pool without fee; anything beyond that is treated as a material change to sizing and routed to commercial review. Add this to the SOW.
3) Approval timing: add SLA for internal approvals (Sales Manager 24h turnaround, Director 48h, VP/CFO 72h) so procurement knows how long an exec exception takes.

On discount bands: I can approve up to 12% on my own. For 12-18% I will escalate to Ben for director-level approval, and Finance must sign off. If Ben wants, we can pre-clear a narrow window for Zephyr (e.g., up to 15%) if they commit to a 36-month tenor instead of 24. That would be a negotiation lever.

Karthik
Head of Sales | Redwood Inference
